## Walkthrough

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant TestSuite as Test Suite
    participant BlockVerifier as BlockVerifier
    participant BlockDatabase as Block Database

    TestSuite->>BlockDatabase: Prepare parent and child blocks
    TestSuite->>BlockVerifier: verifyBlock(childBlock)
    BlockVerifier->>BlockDatabase: Fetch parent block
    alt Parent not found
        BlockVerifier-->>TestSuite: Return ParentNotFound error
    else Parent found
        BlockVerifier->>BlockDatabase: Check parent's posterior state root
        alt State root missing
            BlockVerifier-->>TestSuite: Return StateRootNotFound error
        else State root present
            BlockVerifier->>BlockVerifier: Compare state roots
            alt State roots mismatch
                BlockVerifier-->>TestSuite: Return InvalidStateRoot error
            else State roots match
                BlockVerifier->>BlockVerifier: Validate time slot and extrinsics
                alt Any validation fails
                    BlockVerifier-->>TestSuite: Return corresponding error
                else All checks pass
                    BlockVerifier-->>TestSuite: Return success
                end
            end
        end
    end
```

## Comment by @tomusdrw

@DrEverr no squashing needed.
```
$ git checkout <workingbranch>
$ git reset main --hard # Go back to current main commit (disregard all added commits on working branch)
$ git cherry-pick 5ca69d9 44e64aa 2f399d7 3b2ade0 # only interesting commits
# fix any conficlits and
$ git cherry-pick --continue # commit any conflict fixes
$ git push --force # Replace current remote branch with the one you've built by cherry-picking
```


## Comment by @tomusdrw

```suggestion
    assert.deepStrictEqual(result, Result.error(BlockVerifierError.ParentNotFound, "<details>"));
```

That way it's easier to compare different error conditions, especially if you get `Result.ok` instead of `Result.error`.

By also testing `details` it makes it easier to understand what the test is about.
